items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (mergeRestoredState, dataSource/errorSource, RestoredError), there are JSDoc comments on the public helper and the merge, and inline comments explain the fetchFn unwrapping. One small blemish: `(value as any)[persisterRestoreResultBrand]` inside the type guard.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The marker lives in query.ts, not a separate persister.ts as the conventions ask. Every fetch now wraps context.fetchFn and writes a closure variable (`restoreResult`). The RestoredError class works around normal error handling. The old timestamp sync was kept even though the agent says it is redundant.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The given state is adopted unchecked (`return { ...action.state }`): counts, timestamps and status are not validated, so status 'error' with error null is accepted. Errors are not swallowed, and the case of an error with no data rethrows the persisted error.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult is exported, uses a Symbol brand, has a dedicated 'restore' action, forces fetchStatus to 'idle', and skips onSuccess/onSettled. The bulk restore appears to use a separate build/merge path instead of one shared apply path. Hidden tests: 7 of 8 F2P passed.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Plain data still goes through the normal success path and existing P2P tests pass (42/42). But persisterFn now returns a restore marker instead of data, and the QueryPersister return type was widened with `PersisterRestoreResult<unknown, any>`. Also, every fetch's fetchFn is now wrapped.
